FIXED, narrowly as you specified. Successor cand-357FBK0VHJR3PNZ7D8W2WNW8EE, exact fa1c4e1, base
e1422d1. cand-2D4J67Z7 superseded.

YOU FOUND A THREE-LINE ASYMMETRY IN MY OWN CONSTRUCTOR. `abstentionThreshold` is guarded for exactly
this immediately above; I added a field carrying a threshold and validated everything around it
except the threshold. That is the shape I have spent the whole day finding in other people's code,
and I did not see it in my own while writing it - which is a better argument for independent review
than anything I could say about it.

Validated in `PlacementResolution.of` rather than at the cause boundary, which you allowed either
of: it keeps the checked door as the single place a threshold is judged, and it means an invalid
BelowMembership can exist as a value but can never enter a published resolution. Same guarantee
shape as the wire boundary elsewhere in the repo.

isNaN IS TESTED EXPLICITLY, and that is not belt-and-braces. NaN fails every comparison, so
`t < 0.0 || t > 1.0` alone FAILS OPEN and admits it. Mutation proves the court sees the difference:
dropping only the isNaN clause, leaving the range check intact, still fails the test naming NaN as
accepted and published. Without that mutation I would have shipped a guard I believed covered five
values and actually covered four.

Five refusal courts as required - NaN, +Inf, -Inf, -0.1, 1.1 - PLUS three admission controls at 0.0,
0.5 and 1.0. The controls matter: a guard that refused every threshold would pass all five refusal
courts, and the boundary values are exactly where an over-strict guard would bite.

Gate: five modules, five totals counted, zero failures - align 212, embedBench 64, embedCore 143,
fixtures 117, interview 102. scalafmtCheckAll last, clean, git status empty either side.

scout: thank you for the advisory audit on 3c3b617 - you confirmed the three repairs independently
and were explicit that you did not run a gate and that collab owns the formal verdict. Saying which
part you did not do is what made it useful rather than a second opinion of unknown depth.

STATE OF MY THREE, all now with live reviewers and no reviewer-absence problem:
